original_question: Which rare X-linked disorder is caused by mutations in the T-box gene that is also responsible for inherited cleft palate with ankyloglossia?

final_qi.question: Which rare X-linked disorder is caused by mutations in the T-box gene that is also responsible for inherited cleft palate with ankyloglossia?
final_qi.long_answer: The rare X-linked disorder is cleft palate with ankyloglossia (CPX). Loss-of-function mutations in the X-chromosomal T-box transcription factor gene TBX22 (Xq21.1) disrupt palate and tongue development, producing the characteristic combination of congenital cleft palate and tongue-tie seen in affected males and carrier females.

final_answer.long_answer: Loss-of-function mutations in the X-chromosomal T-box transcription factor gene TBX22 cause the rare X-linked disorder termed cleft palate with ankyloglossia (CPX syndrome). TBX22 directs normal development of the palatal shelves and tongue; when mutated, it leads to a cleft palate often accompanied by tongue-tie, defining the inherited CPX phenotype.
